name: syntax_parser
doc:
SYNTAX - a real deterministic parser (Matt, 2026-10-10: "real syntax parser"). A chart parser
over a hand-written English grammar judges whether a sentence has a valid phrase-structure parse
and returns the tree; sealed through linguistics.LING_VERIFY. Offline, no model. Idempotent.

spec.parse_sentence: the cat sat on the mat

sticks.question: Syntax - a real parse tree, or none

marks.claim: [a real parse, SEALED] 'the cat sat on the mat' has a valid phrase-structure parse (S (NP (DET the) (NOM (N cat))) (VP (V sat) (PP (P on) (NP (DET the) (NOM (N mat)))))), sealed through linguistics.LING_VERIFY. A real chart parser over a hand-written English grammar - offline, no model.
[word salad has none, SEALED] 'cat the sat' has NO valid parse (sealed as correctly not grammatical) - the pinned function words reject it. The parser discriminates structure, not length.

[0 false positives, the limit named] The parser CONFIRMS only a derivation it actually built - a structural fact, never a judgment that the sentence is true or good English. Closed-class words are pinned; open-class POS is a heuristic (no POS lexicon held), so trees are best-effort and a sentence outside the grammar is 'not derivable here', never mis-parsed. Coordination and long-distance dependencies are outside this grammar; a public-domain POS lexicon (Moby) would sharpen it - the next step.

[on the one map - the syntax decline lifted] The comprehensive-linguistics pass had kept syntax closed-class only and declined parsing; this lifts it to a real (if bounded) parser on the linguistics floor (card_floor_indo_european), with the regex/rule verifiers remaining the floor.
